This notebook provides a walkthrough of the analysis and results described in several papers, which as of June 2026 are: 

1) "Generalized Additive Models for Mass Appraisal: Evidence from the Danish Public Property Valuation System" (in review)
2) "Property and Land value Predictions with Generalized Additive Models" (in preparation)
3) "On the Accuracy of Hedonic Real Estate Models" (in preparation)

# 1. Reproducibility and setup 

```{r setup, eval=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)
library(mgcv)
library(gratia) 
library(knitr)
library(patchwork)
library(lubridate)
library(future)
library(future.apply)
library(rlang)
library(stringr)
library(furrr)
library(xgboost)
library(caret)
library(Hmisc)
library(kableExtra)
library(nabor)
library(purrr)
library(ggrastr)
library(ggridges)
library(gridExtra)
library(forcats)
library(pheatmap)
library(viridis)
library(viridisLite)
library(cowplot)
library(scico)
library(scales)

# Global parameters
set.seed(123) # for reproducibility
N <- 4 # number of CV folds
k_spatial = 1500 # initial number of basis functions used in the spatial smooths
k_other = 10 # initial number of basis functions used for other smooths
load <- FALSE # determines whether or not to preload models in the various chunks
plan(multisession, workers = N) #do as much as possible in parallel
options(future.globals.maxSize = 10 * 1024^3) #increase maxSize for future to handle large models

#Create a saved files folder and checkpoints folder is these do not already exist
for (f in c("saved_files", "checkpoints")) {
  if (!dir.exists(f)) {
    dir.create(f, recursive = TRUE)
    message(sprintf("Created folder: %s", f))
  } else {
    message(sprintf("Folder already exists: %s", f))
  }
}
```



# 2. Data 

## 2.1 The dataset
The analysis is based on a dataset of single-family home sales, single-family lot sales and properties in Denmark from 1 January 2014 to 1 January 2024. The dataset, included as a .rds file in this repository, is loaded and inspected below.

```{r Load dataset, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE}

#Externally defined coordinate grid of Denmark
coordinate_grid <- read.csv2("coordinates_ocean_land.csv")

#Load data set
dataset <- readRDS("model_dataset.rds")

#The three types included in the dataset. 
table(dataset$type)

```

## 2.2 Descriptive statistics
In the subsequent cells histograms of selected variables are produced. These histograms are for the raw variables before any imputations and variable conversions take place.

```{r Continuous variables, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=20, fig.height=30}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Labels and plotting parameters
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

get_label <- function(var, labels_vec) {
  
  lbl <- tryCatch(labels_vec[[var]], error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(lbl) || is.na(lbl)) var else lbl
  
}


# Variables for which zeros are excluded from the plotted distribution
# Zero prevalence is still reported in the summary annotation.
exclude_zero_variables <- c("ocean_view", "lake_view", "forest_size")


# Common colours for the three dataset components
type_colors <- c("Property sale" = "#0072B2", "Lot sale" = "#E69F00", "Property" = "#009E73")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot one continuous variable
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

plot_continuous <- function(df, var, label) {

  plot_data <- df %>% select(type, value = all_of(var))

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Convert sales date to decimal year
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  if (var == "sales_date") {
    
    plot_data <- plot_data %>% mutate(value = decimal_date(as.Date(value)))
    
  }


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Summary statistics by dataset component
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  summary_data <- plot_data %>%
                  group_by(type) %>%
                  summarise(n_available = sum(!is.na(value)),
                            missing_pct = 100 * mean(is.na(value)),
                            zero_pct = 100 * mean(value == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
                            .groups = "drop") %>%
                  filter(n_available > 0) %>%
                  mutate(label = paste0(type, ": n = ", 
                         comma(n_available), 
                         ", missing = ", 
                         number(missing_pct, accuracy = 0.1), 
                         "%, zero = ", 
                         number(zero_pct, accuracy = 0.1), "%"))


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Data used for histogram
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  histogram_data <- plot_data %>% filter(!is.na(value), is.finite(value))

  # For zero-inflated environmental variables, show the distribution
  # conditional on a positive value. The fraction of zeros is reported above.
  if (var %in% exclude_zero_variables) {

    histogram_data <- histogram_data %>% filter(value > 0)
    
  }

  if (nrow(histogram_data) == 0L) {return(NULL)}


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Plot
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  p <- ggplot(histogram_data,
              aes(x = value,
                  y = after_stat(density),
                  fill = type,
                  color = type)) +

       geom_histogram(bins = 30,
                      position = "identity",
                      alpha = 0.28,
                      linewidth = 0.35) +

       scale_color_manual(values = type_colors,
                          breaks = names(type_colors),
                          drop = FALSE) +

       scale_fill_manual(values = type_colors,
                         breaks = names(type_colors),
                         drop = FALSE) +

       labs(title = label,
            x = NULL,
            y = "Density",
            color = NULL,
            fill = NULL) +

       theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +

       theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
             panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
             panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
             legend.position = "none")


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Compact summary in upper-right corner
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  summary_data <- summary_data %>%
                  arrange(match(type, names(type_colors))) %>%
                  mutate(vjust = seq(1, by = 1.25, length.out = n()))

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(summary_data))) {

    p <- p + annotate("text",
                      x = Inf,
                      y = Inf,
                      label = summary_data$label[i],
                      hjust = 1.02,
                      vjust = summary_data$vjust[i],
                      size = 3.1,
                      color = type_colors[[summary_data$type[i]]])
  }

  p

}
```

```{r Categorical variables, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=20, fig.height=30}
variables_categorical <- c(house_type = "House type",

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot one categorical variable
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

plot_categorical <- function(df, var, label) {

  plot_data <- df %>% select(type, value = all_of(var))

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Summary information by dataset component
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  summary_data <- plot_data %>%
                  group_by(type) %>%
                  summarise(n_available = sum(!is.na(value)),
                            missing_pct = 100 * mean(is.na(value)),
                            .groups = "drop") %>%
                  filter(n_available > 0) %>%
                  mutate(label = paste0(type,
                                        ": n = ",
                                        comma(n_available),
                                        ", missing = ",
                                        number(missing_pct, accuracy = 0.1),
                                        "%"))


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Category proportions within each dataset component
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  bar_data <- plot_data %>%
              filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
              mutate(value = factor(value)) %>%
              count(type, value, name = "n") %>%
              group_by(type) %>%
              mutate(proportion = n / sum(n)) %>%
              ungroup()

  if (nrow(bar_data) == 0L) {return(NULL)}


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Keep category ordering common across all three dataset components
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  category_order <- bar_data %>%
                    group_by(value) %>%
                    summarise(total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
                    arrange(desc(total)) %>%
                    pull(value) %>%
                    as.character()

  bar_data <- bar_data %>%
              mutate(value = factor(value, levels = category_order))


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Plot
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  p <- ggplot(bar_data,
              aes(x = value,
                  y = proportion,
                  fill = type)) +
       geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
                width = 0.72,
                color = "white",
                linewidth = 0.25) +
       scale_fill_manual(values = type_colors,
                         breaks = names(type_colors),
                         drop = FALSE) +
       scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
       labs(title = label, x = NULL, y = "Share", fill = NULL) +
       theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
       theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
             axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1),
             panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
             panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
             legend.position = "none")


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Compact summary in upper-right corner
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  summary_data <- summary_data %>%
                  arrange(match(type, names(type_colors))) %>%
                  mutate(vjust = seq(1, by = 1.25, length.out = n()))

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(summary_data))) {

    p <- p + annotate("text",
                      x = Inf,
                      y = Inf,
                      label = summary_data$label[i],
                      hjust = 1.02,
                      vjust = summary_data$vjust[i],
                      size = 3.1,
                      color = type_colors[[summary_data$type[i]]])
    
  }

  p
  
}
```

## 2.3 Transformation and imputation
Prior to model fitting, categorical variables are converted to factors, missing values are imputed, and a small number of auxiliary variables are constructed. Continuous reference values are defined centrally and subsequently used both for model interpretation and, where appropriate, for imputation. This ensures that the same values are used consistently throughout preprocessing, model specification, and valuation.

Missing values are treated according to the following rules:

- year_rebuilt: Missing values and rebuilt years before 1970 are replaced by 1970.

- maximum_coverage_percentage: Missing values are imputed to 30%, corresponding to a typical allowed building coverage percentage in Denmark.

- subdivision_size: Missing values are imputed to 700 m$^2$.

- Distance variables: Missing values are replaced by the maximum measurement threshold of the respective variable.

The following auxiliary variables are additionally constructed:

- Numeric sales date: A continuous decimal-year representation of the transaction date.

- Number of subdivisions: Defined as lot size divided by subdivision size, rounded down to the nearest integer and bounded below by one.

```{r Variable conversion and imputation, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reference and imputation values
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable_spec <- tribble(~variable, ~reference, ~imputation,
                         "coordinate_east", 697000, NA,
                         "coordinate_north", 6150000, NA,
                         "sales_date_numeric", 2024, NA,
                         "year_built", 1970, NA,
                         "year_rebuilt", 1970, 1970,
                         "living_space", 140, NA,
                         "lot_size", 800, NA,
                         "number_of_bathrooms", 1, NA,
                         "coast_distance", 1500, 1500,
                         "lake_distance", 500, 500,
                         "stream_distance", 1000, 1000,
                         "road_distance", 2000, 2000,
                         "highway_distance", 2000, 2000,
                         "train_station_distance", 2000, 2000,
                         "railway_distance", 1000, 1000,
                         "windturbine_distance", 3000, 3000,
                         "ocean_view", 0, NA,
                         "lake_view", 0, NA,
                         "forest_size", 0, NA,
                         "maximum_coverage_percentage", 30, 30,
                         "subdivision_size", 700, 700)

reference_values <- setNames(variable_spec$reference, variable_spec$variable)
imputation_values <- setNames(variable_spec$imputation, variable_spec$variable)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Factor reference levels
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

factor_references <- c(municipality_type = "Provincial",
                       municipality = "Køge",
                       house_type = "Detached",
                       roof_type = "Fiber cement",
                       wall_type = "Brick",
                       heating_type = "District heating")

for (v in names(factor_references)) {dataset[[v]] <- relevel(factor(dataset[[v]]), ref = factor_references[[v]])}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Auxiliary date variable
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

dataset <- dataset %>% mutate(sales_date = as.Date(sales_date), sales_date_numeric = decimal_date(sales_date))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Missing values
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Rebuilt year requires the additional rule that years before 1970 are replaced

dataset <- dataset %>% mutate(year_rebuilt = if_else(is.na(year_rebuilt) | year_rebuilt < reference_values[["year_rebuilt"]],
                              reference_values[["year_rebuilt"]],
                              year_rebuilt))

# Remaining variables with explicit imputation values

variables_to_impute <- variable_spec %>% 
                       filter(!is.na(imputation), variable != "year_rebuilt") %>%
                       pull(variable)

for (v in variables_to_impute) {dataset[[v]] <- replace_na(dataset[[v]], imputation_values[[v]])}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Auxiliary variables
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

dataset <- dataset %>% mutate(number_of_divisions = pmax(1, floor(lot_size / subdivision_size)))

# Separate property sales, lot sales and valuation properties
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

dataset_property_sales <- dataset %>%
                          filter(type == "Property sale") %>%
                          mutate(type = factor(type, levels = c("Lot sale", "Property sale")),
                                 type_ordered = ordered(type, levels = c("Lot sale", "Property sale")))

dataset_lot_sales <- dataset %>% 
                     filter(type == "Lot sale") %>%
                     mutate(type = factor(type, levels = c("Lot sale", "Property sale")),
                            type_ordered = ordered(type, levels = c("Lot sale", "Property sale")))

dataset_properties <- dataset %>% 
                      filter(type == "Property") %>%
                      mutate(sales_date_numeric = reference_values[["sales_date_numeric"]])

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Check that there are no remaining NA values among property sales
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
which(is.na(dataset_property_sales))

```

## 2.4 Cross-validation design 
The property sales and lot sales are partitioned into four cross-validation folds ($K=4$). The resulting folds are subsequently used both to estimate out-of-sample predictive performance and to assess the robustness of the fitted models to perturbations of the training data. The same property-sale folds are used for all three model specifications.

```{r Cross-validation, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, results = 'hide'}

assign_cv_folds <- function(data, N, seed = 123) {

  set.seed(seed)

  data %>% 
  group_by(municipality) %>% #try to keep at least one municipality in each fold for parametric model
  mutate(validation_set = sample(rep(seq_len(N), length.out = n())), .rand = runif(n())) %>% 
  ungroup()

}

dataset_property_sales_cv <- assign_cv_folds(dataset_property_sales, N = N, seed = 123)
dataset_lot_sales_cv <- assign_cv_folds(dataset_lot_sales, N = N, seed = 123)

table(dataset_property_sales_cv$validation_set, useNA = "ifany")
table(dataset_lot_sales_cv$validation_set, useNA = "ifany")

```


# 3. Paper I: "Generalized Additive Models for Mass Appraisal: Evidence from the Danish Public Property Valuation System" 

## 3.1 Model specification and fitting
Three model specifications are estimated. The first specification is a conventional parametric hedonic benchmark in which continuous property and location characteristics enter linearly, geographical variation is represented by municipality fixed effects, and categorical characteristics enter through reference-coded factor effects. Second, a nationwide GAM replaces the parametric functional forms with smooth functions while retaining common characteristic effects across Denmark. Third, the proposed GAM additionally allows selected temporal, structural, and categorical effects to vary across municipality types. All three specifications use a Tweedie response distribution with a logarithmic link and are fitted using identical cross-validation folds. For each specification, one model is fitted for every cross-validation fold using the remaining $K-1$ folds as the training sample. To isolate sensitivity to changes in the training population, each model is fitted using the complete training sample in a single processing chunk (chunk.size = nrow(training_subset)). This reduces numerical variation associated with chunk-wise updating, making differences across cross-validation fits more directly interpretable as sensitivity to perturbations of the training data (see https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/659490/reproducibility-of-bam-mgcv-algorithm).

#### Parametric hedonic benchmark 

```{r Parametric benchmark, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper for centered linear terms
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

center_term <- function(variable) {

  sprintf("I(%s - %s)", variable, reference_values[[variable]])
  
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Classical parametric hedonic benchmark
#
# Continuous covariates enter linearly around the common reference values.
# Geographic variation is represented by municipality fixed effects.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

parametric_terms <- c(

  # Geographic fixed effects
  "municipality",

  # National time trend
  center_term("sales_date_numeric"),

  # Structural characteristics
  center_term("year_built"),
  center_term("year_rebuilt"),
  center_term("living_space"),
  center_term("lot_size"),
  center_term("number_of_bathrooms"),

  # Distance variables
  center_term("coast_distance"),
  center_term("lake_distance"),
  center_term("stream_distance"),
  center_term("road_distance"),
  center_term("highway_distance"),
  center_term("train_station_distance"),
  center_term("railway_distance"),
  center_term("windturbine_distance"),

  # Environmental characteristics
  center_term("ocean_view"),
  center_term("lake_view"),
  center_term("forest_size"),

  # Categorical structural characteristics
  "house_type",
  "roof_type",
  "wall_type",
  "heating_type"
  
)


parametric_formula <- as.formula(paste("sales_price ~", paste(parametric_terms, collapse = " + ")))


```

#### Nationwide GAM 

```{r GAM 1, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}

make_gam1_formula <- function(k_spatial, k_other, ref) {

  as.formula(paste0("sales_price ~ ",
                    "s(coordinate_east, coordinate_north, ", "k = ", k_spatial, ", ", "pc = c(", ref[["coordinate_east"]], ", ", ref[["coordinate_north"]], ")) + ",
                    "s(sales_date_numeric, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["sales_date_numeric"]], ") + ",
                    "s(year_built, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["year_built"]], ") + ",
                    "s(year_rebuilt, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["year_rebuilt"]], ") + ",
                    "s(living_space, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["living_space"]], ") + ",
                    "s(lot_size, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["lot_size"]], ") + ",
                    "s(coast_distance, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["coast_distance"]], ") + ",
                    "s(lake_distance, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["lake_distance"]], ") + ",
                    "s(stream_distance, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["stream_distance"]], ") + ",
                    "s(road_distance, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["road_distance"]], ") + ",
                    "s(highway_distance, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["highway_distance"]], ") + ",
                    "s(train_station_distance, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["train_station_distance"]], ") + ",
                    "s(railway_distance, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["railway_distance"]], ") + ",
                    "s(windturbine_distance, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["windturbine_distance"]], ") + ",
                    "s(ocean_view, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["ocean_view"]], ") + ",
                    "s(lake_view, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["lake_view"]], ") + ",
                    "s(forest_size, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["forest_size"]], ") + ",
                    "s(number_of_bathrooms, k = 2, ", "pc = ", ref[["number_of_bathrooms"]], ") + ",
                    "house_type + ",
                    "roof_type + ",
                    "wall_type + ",
                    "heating_type"))

}

gam1_formula <- make_gam1_formula(k_spatial = k_spatial, k_other = k_other, ref = reference_values)

```

#### Municipality-type interacting GAM 

```{r GAM 2, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}

make_gam2_formula <- function(k_spatial, k_other, ref) {

  as.formula(paste0("sales_price ~ ",
                    "s(coordinate_east, coordinate_north, ", "k = ", k_spatial, ", ", "pc = c(", ref[["coordinate_east"]], ", ", ref[["coordinate_north"]], ")) + ",
                    "s(sales_date_numeric, k = ", k_other, ", by = municipality_type, ", "pc = ", ref[["sales_date_numeric"]], ") + ",
                    "s(year_built, k = ", k_other, ", by = municipality_type, ", "pc = ", ref[["year_built"]], ") + ",
                    "s(year_rebuilt, k = ", k_other, ", by = municipality_type, ", "pc = ", ref[["year_rebuilt"]], ") + ",
                    "s(living_space, k = ", k_other, ", by = municipality_type, ", "pc = ", ref[["living_space"]], ") + ",
                    "s(lot_size, k = ", k_other, ", by = municipality_type, ", "pc = ", ref[["lot_size"]], ") + ",
                    "s(coast_distance, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["coast_distance"]], ") + ",
                    "s(lake_distance, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["lake_distance"]], ") + ",
                    "s(stream_distance, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["stream_distance"]], ") + ",
                    "s(road_distance, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["road_distance"]], ") + ",
                    "s(highway_distance, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["highway_distance"]], ") + ",
                    "s(train_station_distance, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["train_station_distance"]], ") + ",
                    "s(railway_distance, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["railway_distance"]], ") + ",
                    "s(windturbine_distance, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["windturbine_distance"]], ") + ",
                    "s(ocean_view, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["ocean_view"]], ") + ",
                    "s(lake_view, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["lake_view"]], ") + ",
                    "s(forest_size, k = ", k_other, ", pc = ", ref[["forest_size"]], ") + ",
                    "s(number_of_bathrooms, k = 2, ", "by = municipality_type, ", "pc = ", ref[["number_of_bathrooms"]], ") + ",
                    "house_type * municipality_type + ",
                    "roof_type * municipality_type + ",
                    "wall_type * municipality_type + ",
                    "heating_type * municipality_type"))

}


gam2_formula <- make_gam2_formula(k_spatial = k_spatial, k_other = k_other, ref = reference_values)

```

#### Model fitting 

```{r Property model fitting, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generic function for fitting one cross-validation fold
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

fit_fold <- function(i,
                     data,
                     formula,
                     fraction = 1.0,
                     checkpoint_prefix = NULL,
                     save_checkpoint = TRUE) {

  training_subset <- data %>% filter(validation_set != i)

  if (fraction < 1.0) {

    training_subset <- training_subset %>%
                       group_by(municipality_type) %>%
                       arrange(.rand, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
                       slice_head(prop = fraction) %>%
                       ungroup()
  }

  model <- bam(formula = formula,
               data = training_subset,
               chunk.size = nrow(training_subset),
               family = tw(link = "log"),
               method = "fREML")

  if (save_checkpoint && !is.null(checkpoint_prefix)) {

    filename <- sprintf("%s_fold%d_frac%.2f.rds",
                        checkpoint_prefix,
                        i,
                        fraction)

    saveRDS(model, file = file.path("checkpoints", filename))
    
  }

  model
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generic function for fitting all cross-validation folds
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

fit_ensemble <- function(data,
                         formula,
                         N,
                         fraction = 1.0,
                         checkpoint_prefix = NULL) {

  models <- future_lapply(seq_len(N),
                          function(i) {
                          fit_fold(i = i,
                                   data = data,
                                   formula = formula,
                                   fraction = fraction,
                                   checkpoint_prefix = checkpoint_prefix)})

  names(models) <- paste0("Model", seq_len(N))

  models
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fit or load models
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

if (load) {

  models_parametric <- readRDS("saved_files/models_parametric.rds")
  models_gam1 <- readRDS("saved_files/models_gam1.rds")
  models_gam2 <- readRDS("saved_files/models_gam2.rds")

} else {

  models_parametric <- fit_ensemble(data = dataset_property_sales_cv,
                                    formula = parametric_formula,
                                    N = N,
                                    fraction = 1.0,
                                    checkpoint_prefix = "parametric")
  
  saveRDS(models_parametric, "saved_files/models_parametric.rds")

  models_gam1 <- fit_ensemble(data = dataset_property_sales_cv,
                              formula = gam1_formula,
                              N = N,
                              fraction = 1.0,
                              checkpoint_prefix = "gam1")
  
  saveRDS(models_gam1, "saved_files/models_gam1.rds")

  models_gam2 <- fit_ensemble(data = dataset_property_sales_cv,
                              formula = gam2_formula,
                              N = N,
                              fraction = 1.0,
                              checkpoint_prefix = "gam2")

  saveRDS(models_gam2, "saved_files/models_gam2.rds")
  
}

```

## 3.2 Partial effects

#### Spatial smooths 
The code below extracts the spatial smooth for each model and plots it alongside the log-scale standard error. The plotting relies on a premade spatial grid of Denmark, where ocean and land are marked. 

```{r Spatial smooths property models, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, results = 'hide', fig.width=20, fig.height=30}

# 1a) Predict once per model and store results
prediction_results <- future_lapply(seq_along(models_gam2), function(i) {
  model <- models_gam2[[i]]
  model_data <- model.frame(model)
  grid <- coordinate_grid

  for (var in setdiff(all.vars(formula(model)), names(grid))) {
    x <- model_data[[var]]
    if (is.factor(x)) {
      grid[[var]] <- factor(rep(levels(x)[1], nrow(grid)), levels = levels(x))
    } else {
      grid[[var]] <- 0
    }
  }

  terms <- predict.gam(model, grid, type = "terms", se.fit = TRUE)
  df_predictions <- as.data.frame(terms$fit)
  df_se <- as.data.frame(terms$se.fit)

  effect <- df_predictions$`s(coordinate_east,coordinate_north)`
  se <- df_se$`s(coordinate_east,coordinate_north)`
  effect[grid$ocean] <- NA
  se[grid$ocean] <- NA

  grid$effect_coordinates <- effect
  grid$se_coordinates <- se

  list(model_name = names(models_gam2)[i],
       grid = grid)
})


# 1b) Compute SD across models (per grid cell) ---
effects_mat <- do.call(cbind, lapply(prediction_results, function(x) x$grid$effect_coordinates))
base_grid   <- prediction_results[[1]]$grid

se_across_models <- apply(effects_mat, 1, sd, na.rm = TRUE)
se_across_models[base_grid$ocean] <- NA

# 2. Global ranges (normalized across everything) ---
# Effects: symmetric across *all model* effects
all_effects <- unlist(lapply(prediction_results, function(x) x$grid$effect_coordinates))
max_abs_effect <- max(abs(all_effects), na.rm = TRUE)
effect_limits  <- c(-max_abs_effect, max_abs_effect)

# SEs: include per-model SEs AND the across-models SD
all_ses_models <- unlist(lapply(prediction_results, function(x) x$grid$se_coordinates))
se_limits <- c(0, max(c(all_ses_models, se_across_models), na.rm = TRUE))  # SEs are >= 0

# 3. Plotting function (adds land/ocean outline) ---
plot_model_terms_from_grid <- function(grid, model_name, effect_range, se_range) {

  plot_effect <- ggplot(data = grid) +
                 geom_tile(aes(coordinate_east, coordinate_north, fill = effect_coordinates)) +
                 labs(x = "", y = "") +
                 scale_fill_scico(palette = "vik",
                                  name = paste("Partial effect", sub("^Model", "Model ", model_name)),
                                  na.value = "white",
                                  limits = effect_range) +
                 geom_contour(aes(x = coordinate_east, y = coordinate_north, z = as.numeric(!ocean)),
                              color = "black", 
                              size = 0.4) +
                 coord_fixed() +
                 theme_void() +
                 theme(text = element_text(size = 12),
                       legend.position = c(0.85, 0.75),
                       legend.title = element_text(size = 9, margin = margin(b = 5)),
                       legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
                       legend.title.align = 0.5)
  
  model_label <- sub("^Model", "Model ", model_name)

  plot_se <- ggplot(data = grid) +
             geom_tile(aes(coordinate_east, coordinate_north, fill = se_coordinates)) +
             labs(x = "", y = "") +
             scale_fill_scico(
             palette = "vik",
             name = bquote(sigma[.(model_label)]),
             na.value = "white",
             limits = se_range) +
             geom_contour(aes(x = coordinate_east, y = coordinate_north, z = as.numeric(!ocean)),
                          color = "black", 
                          size = 0.4) +
             coord_fixed() +
             theme_void() +
             theme(text = element_text(size = 12),
                   legend.position = c(0.85, 0.75),
                   legend.title = element_text(size = 9, margin = margin(b = 5)),
                   legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
                   legend.title.align = 0.5)

  list(effect = plot_effect, se = plot_se)
}

# 4. Build plots for each model (effect + SE) ---
plot_lists <- lapply(prediction_results, function(result) {
  
  plot_model_terms_from_grid(result$grid, 
                             result$model_name,
                             effect_range = effect_limits,
                             se_range     = se_limits)
  
})

plot_spatial_smooths <- unlist(plot_lists, recursive = FALSE)

# 5. ONE extra plot: SD of effects across models (uses same se_limits) ---

base_grid2$se_across_models <- se_across_models  # <- bake it into the data

                               color = "black",

                  theme_void() +
                  theme(text = element_text(size = 12),
                        legend.position = c(0.85, 0.75),
                        legend.title = element_text(size = 9, margin = margin(b = 5)),
                        legend.text = element_text(size = 9),

plot_spatial_smooths <- c(plot_spatial_smooths, list(plot_sd_across))
```

```{r Other smooth effects property models, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, results = 'hide', fig.width=20, fig.height=30}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: extract centred linear coefficient from parametric benchmark
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

get_parametric_beta <- function(model, var) {

  coef_names <- names(coef(model))

  candidates <- coef_names[startsWith(coef_names, paste0("I(", var, " - "))]

  if (length(candidates) != 1) {return(NA_real_)}

  unname(coef(model)[candidates])
}


for (var in names(smooth_variables)) {

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Municipality-type interacting GAM: all four ensemble members
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  smooth_dfs_gam2 <- lapply(
    names(models_gam2),
    function(model_name) {

      mod <- models_gam2[[model_name]]

      df <- tryCatch(
        smooth_estimates(
          mod,
          smooth = paste0("s(", var, ")"),
          partial_match = TRUE
        ),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )

      if (!is.null(df)) {df$Model <- sub("^Model", "Model ", model_name)}

      df
    }
  )

  smooth_dfs_gam2 <- Filter(Negate(is.null), smooth_dfs_gam2)

  if (length(smooth_dfs_gam2) == 0) {next}

  combined_df <- bind_rows(smooth_dfs_gam2)

    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  nationwide_points <- NULL

  if (!is.null(nationwide_df) && nrow(nationwide_df) > 0) {

                        nrow(nationwide_df),

    nationwide_points <- nationwide_df[point_idx, ]
  }


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Parametric benchmark: Model 1 only
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  parametric_points <- NULL

  beta <- get_parametric_beta(models_parametric[["Model1"]], var)

  if (!is.na(beta) && var %in% names(reference_values)) {

    x_parametric <- seq(min(combined_df[[var]], na.rm = TRUE),
                        max(combined_df[[var]], na.rm = TRUE),
                        length.out = parametric_n_points)

    parametric_points <- tibble(x = x_parametric,
                                effect = beta * (x_parametric - reference_values[[var]]))
  }


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  has_by <- any(!is.na(combined_df$.by))

                      color = .data[[by_var_name]],

        labs(title = plot_title,
             x = smooth_variables[[var]],
             y = "Partial effect",
             color = "Municipality type",
             fill = "Municipality type",
             linetype = "Model") +

        scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "Municipality type") +

        scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "Municipality type")


  # ==========================================================================
  # Nationwide smooths within the interacting GAM
  # ==========================================================================

  } else {

    p <- ggplot() +

         # Confidence interval for GAM2 Model 1
         geom_ribbon(data = subset(combined_df, Model == "Model 1"),
         aes(x = .data[[var]],
             ymin = .estimate - 1.96 * .se,
             ymax = .estimate + 1.96 * .se),
         alpha = 0.25,
         color = NA) +

         # Nationwide smooths from the interacting GAM
         geom_line(data = combined_df,
                   aes(x = .data[[var]],
                       y = .estimate,
                       linetype = Model,
                       group = Model),
                   color = "black",
                   linewidth = 1) +

          labs(title = plot_title,
               x = smooth_variables[[var]],
               y = "Partial effect",
               linetype = "Model")
  }


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Nationwide GAM comparison
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  if (!is.null(nationwide_points)) {

    p <- p + geom_point(data = nationwide_points,

                        color = "black",

  }


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Parametric benchmark comparison
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  if (!is.null(parametric_points)) {

    p <- p + geom_point(data = parametric_points,
                        aes(x = x, y = effect),
                        inherit.aes = FALSE,
                        color = "black",
                        size = parametric_point_size,
                        shape = 8,
                        show.legend = FALSE)
  }


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Common line-type scale and legends
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  p <- p + scale_linetype_manual(values = model_linetypes,
                                 name = "Model",
                                 breaks = names(model_linetypes)) +

           guides(fill = "none", 
                  color = guide_legend(order = 1),
                  linetype = guide_legend(order = 2, 
                                          override.aes = list(color = "black", linewidth = 1)))

  plot_smooths[[var]] <- p
}
```

#### Factor effects
The code below extracts and plots the factor effects of the trained GAM-models. A point is shown for the effect of each model but error bars are shown only for Model 1. 

```{r Factor effects property models, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, results = 'hide', fig.width=20, fig.height=20}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Factor variables
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

factor_variables <- c(house_type = "House type",
                      municipality_type = "Municipality type",
                      roof_type = "Roof type",
                      wall_type = "Wall type",
                      heating_type = "Heating type")

point_size <- 2.5
errorbar_width <- 0.22
errorbar_linewidth <- 0.6

# Comparison markers
nationwide_shape <- 4
parametric_shape <- 8
comparison_point_size <- 2.5


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

get_model1 <- function(models) {models[[which(gsub("\\s+", "", names(models)) == "Model1")]]}


factor_effect <- function(model, variable, by = NULL) {

  mf <- model.frame(model)

  # Start from a valid observation and put all factors at reference levels
  base <- mf[1, , drop = FALSE]

  for (v in names(base)) {

    if (is.factor(mf[[v]])) {

      base[[v]] <- factor(levels(mf[[v]])[1], levels = levels(mf[[v]]))
      
    }
  }


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Prediction grid
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  if (is.null(by)) {

    nd <- base[rep(1, nlevels(mf[[variable]])), , drop = FALSE]
    nd[[variable]] <- factor(levels(mf[[variable]]), levels = levels(mf[[variable]]))

  } else {

    g <- expand.grid(var = levels(mf[[variable]]),
                     by = levels(mf[[by]]),
                     KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

    nd <- base[rep(1, nrow(g)), , drop = FALSE]

    nd[[variable]] <- factor(g$var, levels = levels(mf[[variable]]))

    nd[[by]] <- factor(g$by, levels = levels(mf[[by]]))
    
  }


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Relevant parametric coefficients only
  #
  # model$nsdf excludes smooth coefficients in the GAMs.
  # For the fully parametric model this corresponds to the full coefficient
  # block.
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  param_idx <- seq_len(model$nsdf)
  cn <- names(coef(model))[param_idx]

  keep <- vapply(cn,
                 
    function(x) {
      parts <- strsplit(x, ":", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
      any(startsWith(parts, variable))},
    logical(1)
  )

  idx <- param_idx[keep]


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Exact effect and standard error
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  if (length(idx) == 0L) {

    effect <- rep(0, nrow(nd))
    se <- rep(0, nrow(nd))

  } else {

    X <- predict(model, newdata = nd, type = "lpmatrix")[, idx, drop = FALSE]

    beta <- coef(model)[idx]

    V <- vcov(model)[idx, idx, drop = FALSE]

    effect <- as.vector(X %*% beta)

    variance <- rowSums((X %*% V) * X)

    se <- sqrt(pmax(variance, 0))
    
  }

  nd %>% mutate(effect = effect, se = se, lower = effect - 1.96 * se, upper = effect + 1.96 * se) %>%
         select(any_of(c(variable, by)), effect, se, lower, upper) %>%
         mutate(term = variable)
}


# ==============================================================================
# GAM2: all four cross-validation models
# ==============================================================================

df_factors_gam2 <- bind_rows(lapply(names(models_gam2),
                                    
    function(model_name) {

      model <- models_gam2[[model_name]]

      bind_rows(lapply(names(factor_variables),
          
            function(variable) {

            if (!(variable %in% all.vars(formula(model)))) {return(NULL)}

            by <- if (variable == "municipality_type") {NULL} else {"municipality_type"}

            factor_effect(model, variable, by) %>%
            mutate(Model = sub("^Model", "Model ", model_name))
          }
        )
      )
    }
  )
)

# Nationwide GAM: Model 1 only

# ==============================================================================
# Plotting function for factors shared with the GAMs
# ==============================================================================

plot_factor_effect <- function(term_name) {

  g2 <- df_factors_gam2 %>%
        filter(term == term_name)

  g1 <- df_factors_gam1 %>%
        filter(term == term_name)

  par <- df_factors_parametric %>%
         filter(term == term_name)

  if (nrow(g2) == 0L) {return(NULL)}

  model_shapes <- c("Model 1" = 16,
                    "Model 2" = 17,
                    "Model 3" = 15,
                    "Model 4" = 3)

  interacted <- (term_name != "municipality_type" && "municipality_type" %in% names(g2))

  pos <- position_dodge(width = if (interacted) 0.65 else 0.55)


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Municipality-type-specific structural effects
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  if (interacted) {

    p <- ggplot(g2,
                aes(x = .data[[term_name]],
                    y = effect,
                    color = municipality_type,
                    shape = Model,
                    group = interaction(Model, municipality_type)))

  } else {

    # Municipality-type main effect
    p <- ggplot(g2,
                aes(x = .data[[term_name]],
                    y = effect,
                    color = .data[[term_name]],
                    shape = Model,
                    group = Model))
  }


  p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = 0,
                      linewidth = 0.4,
                      linetype = "dashed") +

    # Confidence intervals for GAM2 Model 1
    geom_errorbar(data = g2 %>% filter(Model == "Model 1"),
                  aes(ymin = lower,
                      ymax = upper),
                  position = pos,
                  width = errorbar_width,
                  linewidth = errorbar_linewidth) +

    # All four GAM2 models
    geom_point(position = pos, size = point_size) +

    scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "Municipality type")


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Nationwide GAM: Model 1
  #
  # Black crosses, excluded from legends
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  if (nrow(g1) > 0L) {

    p <- p + geom_point(data = g1,
                        aes(x = .data[[term_name]],
                            y = effect),
                        inherit.aes = FALSE,
                        color = "black",
                        shape = nationwide_shape,
                        size = comparison_point_size,
                        stroke = 0.8,
                        show.legend = FALSE)
  }


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Parametric benchmark: Model 1
  #
  # Black asterisks, excluded from legends
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  if (nrow(par) > 0L) {

    p <- p + geom_point(data = par,
                        aes(x = .data[[term_name]],
                            y = effect),
                        inherit.aes = FALSE,
                        color = "black",
                        shape = parametric_shape,
                        size = comparison_point_size,
                        stroke = 0.8,
                        show.legend = FALSE)
  }


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Formatting
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  p + coord_flip() +

      scale_shape_manual(values = model_shapes, name = "Model") +

      labs(x = NULL,
           y = "Partial effect",
           title = paste("Partial effect of", tolower(factor_variables[[term_name]]))) +

      guides(color = guide_legend(order = 1),
      shape = guide_legend(order = 2, override.aes = list(color = "black", size = point_size))) +

      theme(axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1))
  
}
```

## 3.3 Illustrative valuations
The code below performs valuations using the fitted models of a set of chosen example properties. 

```{r Interpretation property models, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE}

# The code below selects five actual valuation properties, chosen to illustrate
# different characteristics and housing-market contexts:
#
#   A Rural        : old house
#   B Capital      : close to the coast, in Gentofte
#   C Commuter     : large living space, on Fyn
#   D Large city   : recently constructed
#   E Provincial   : large lot, preferably in Vestjylland
#
# Moderately extreme quantiles are used instead of absolute extrema to avoid
# selecting unusual edge cases. The selected properties are valued with all
# four fitted municipality-type GAMs and decomposed into multiplicative
# location and structural adjustments.


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Select five illustrative valuation properties
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

illustrative_selection <- tibble(property_label = LETTERS[1:5],
                                 municipality_type = c("Rural",
                                                       "Capital",
                                                       "Commuter",
                                                       "Large city",
                                                       "Provincial"),
                                 selection_variable = c("year_built",
                                                        "coast_distance",
                                                        "living_space",
                                                        "year_built",
                                                        "lot_size"),
                                 target_quantile = c(0.10, 0.10, 0.90, 0.90, 0.90),
                                 description = c("Old house",
                                                 "Close to coast",
                                                 "Large house",
                                                 "New house",
                                                 "Large lot")
)


select_illustrative_property <- function(data,
                                         municipality_type_value,
                                         selection_variable,
                                         target_quantile) {

  candidates <- data %>% filter(as.character(municipality_type) == municipality_type_value)


  # Capital example: use Gentofte
  if (municipality_type_value == "Capital") {

    candidates_restricted <- candidates %>% filter(tolower(as.character(municipality)) == "gentofte")

    if (nrow(candidates_restricted) > 0) {candidates <- candidates_restricted}
  }


  # Commuter example: use Fyn
  if (municipality_type_value == "Commuter") {

    candidates_restricted <- candidates %>% filter(tolower(as.character(province)) == "fyn")

    if (nrow(candidates_restricted) > 0) {candidates <- candidates_restricted}
  }


  # Provincial example: use Vestjylland
  if (municipality_type_value == "Provincial") {

    candidates_restricted <- candidates %>% filter(tolower(as.character(province)) == "vestjylland")

    if (nrow(candidates_restricted) > 0) {candidates <- candidates_restricted}
  }


  target_value <- quantile(candidates[[selection_variable]],
                           probs = target_quantile,
                           na.rm = TRUE,
                           names = FALSE)


  candidates %>% 
  mutate(distance_to_target = abs(.data[[selection_variable]] - target_value)) %>%
  slice_min(distance_to_target, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  select(-distance_to_target)
  
}


illustrative_properties <- pmap_dfr(illustrative_selection,

  function(property_label,
           municipality_type,
           selection_variable,
           target_quantile,
           description) {

    selected <- select_illustrative_property(data = dataset_properties,
                                             municipality_type_value = municipality_type,
                                             selection_variable = selection_variable,
                                             target_quantile = target_quantile)

    selected %>% mutate(property_label = property_label,
                        example = municipality_type,
                        example_description = description,
                        selection_variable = selection_variable,
                        selection_quantile = target_quantile,
                        .before = 1)
  }
)



# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Helper for summing model terms
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

sum_matching_terms <- function(term_df, pattern) {

  cols <- grep(pattern, names(term_df), value = TRUE)

  if (length(cols) == 0L) {return(rep(0, nrow(term_df)))}

  rowSums(term_df[, cols, drop = FALSE])
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Function for valuation decomposition
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

make_interpretation_results <- function(model,
                                        model_name,
                                        properties) {

  model_data <- model.frame(model)

  grid <- properties


  # Ensure factor levels correspond to those used in the fitted model
  for (var in intersect(names(grid), names(model_data))) {

    if (is.factor(model_data[[var]])) {

      grid[[var]] <- factor(grid[[var]], levels = levels(model_data[[var]]))
      
    }
  }


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Predict individual model terms
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  terms <- as.data.frame(predict.gam(model, newdata = grid, type = "terms"))


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Multiplicative adjustments
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  adjustments <- tibble(

    standard_price = rep(exp(coef(model)[1]), nrow(grid)),


    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Location characteristics
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------

    adjustment_coordinates = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(coordinate_east,coordinate_north\\)$")),

    adjustment_sales_date = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(sales_date_numeric\\):municipality_type")),

    adjustment_coast_distance = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(coast_distance\\)$")),

    adjustment_lake_distance = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(lake_distance\\)$")),

    adjustment_stream_distance = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(stream_distance\\)$")),

    adjustment_road_distance = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(road_distance\\)$")),

    adjustment_highway_distance = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(highway_distance\\)$")),

    adjustment_train_station_distance = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(train_station_distance\\)$")),

    adjustment_railway_distance = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(railway_distance\\)$")),

    adjustment_windturbine_distance = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(windturbine_distance\\)$")),

    adjustment_ocean_view = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(ocean_view\\)$")),

    adjustment_lake_view = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(lake_view\\)$")),

    adjustment_forest_size = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(forest_size\\)$")),

    adjustment_municipality_type = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^municipality_type$")),

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Structural characteristics
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------

    adjustment_year_built = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(year_built\\):municipality_type")),

    adjustment_year_rebuilt = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(year_rebuilt\\):municipality_type")),

    adjustment_living_space = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(living_space\\):municipality_type")),

    adjustment_lot_size = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(lot_size\\):municipality_type")),

    adjustment_number_of_bathrooms = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^s\\(number_of_bathrooms\\):municipality_type")),

    adjustment_house_type = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^house_type$|^house_type:municipality_type$|^municipality_type:house_type$")),

    adjustment_roof_type = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^roof_type$|^roof_type:municipality_type$|^municipality_type:roof_type$")),

    adjustment_wall_type = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^wall_type$|^wall_type:municipality_type$|^municipality_type:wall_type$")),

    adjustment_heating_type = exp(sum_matching_terms(terms, "^heating_type$|^heating_type:municipality_type$|^municipality_type:heating_type$")))


    # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Aggregate location and structural adjustments
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

    adjustments <- adjustments %>%
                   mutate(adjustment_location =
                          adjustment_coordinates *
                          adjustment_coast_distance *
                          adjustment_lake_distance *
                          adjustment_stream_distance *
                          adjustment_road_distance *
                          adjustment_highway_distance *
                          adjustment_train_station_distance *
                          adjustment_railway_distance *
                          adjustment_windturbine_distance *
                          adjustment_ocean_view *
                          adjustment_lake_view *
                          adjustment_forest_size *
                          adjustment_municipality_type,


                          adjustment_structural =
                          adjustment_year_built *
                          adjustment_year_rebuilt *
                          adjustment_living_space *
                          adjustment_lot_size *
                          adjustment_number_of_bathrooms *
                          adjustment_house_type *
                          adjustment_roof_type *
                          adjustment_wall_type *
                          adjustment_heating_type,

                          adjustment_total = adjustment_location * adjustment_structural,

                          predicted_price = standard_price * adjustment_sales_date * adjustment_total)


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Direct prediction for verification
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  direct_prediction <- as.vector(predict.gam(model, newdata = grid, type = "response"))


  adjustments <- adjustments %>%
                 mutate(direct_prediction = direct_prediction,
                        prediction_difference = predicted_price - direct_prediction,
                        relative_prediction_difference = prediction_difference / direct_prediction)


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Output
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  bind_cols(grid, adjustments) %>%
  mutate(Model = model_name, .before = 1)
  
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Run all four municipality-type GAMs
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

results_all_models <- bind_rows(
  
  lapply(names(models_gam2),

    function(model_name) {

      make_interpretation_results(
        model = models_gam2[[model_name]],
        model_name = model_name,
        properties = illustrative_properties
      )
    }
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Verify decomposition
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

decomposition_check <- results_all_models %>%
                       summarise(max_absolute_difference = max(abs(prediction_difference), na.rm = TRUE),
                                 max_relative_difference = max(abs(relative_prediction_difference), na.rm = TRUE))


print(decomposition_check)

stopifnot(decomposition_check$max_relative_difference < 1e-8)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6d. Function constructing one decomposition table per property
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

make_decomposition_table <- function(property) {

  property_data <- interpretation_decomposition %>%
                   filter(property_label == property) %>%
                   select(Model, all_of(names(decomposition_variables))) %>%
                   pivot_longer(cols = -Model,
                                names_to = "variable",
                                values_to = "value") %>%
                   mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(decomposition_variables)),
                          Adjustment = decomposition_variables[as.character(variable)]) %>%
                   select(Model, variable, Adjustment, value) %>%
                   pivot_wider(names_from = Model,
                               values_from = value) %>%
                   arrange(variable) %>%
                   select(-variable)


  property_info <- illustrative_properties %>%
                   filter(property_label == property)

  property_info <- property_info[1, ]


  property_description <- paste0(property,
                                 ": ",
                                 property_info$example_description,
                                 " in ",
                                 as.character(property_info$municipality))


  # Row positions:
  #
  # 1--2   Reference/time
  # 3--15  Location effects
  # 16--24 Structural effects
  # 25--28 Aggregate results

  latex_table <- kable(property_data,
                       format = "latex",
                       booktabs = TRUE,
                       linesep = "",
                       digits = 2,
                       escape = TRUE,
                       caption = paste0("Complete valuation decomposition for property ",
                                        property,
                                        " (",
                                        property_info$example_description,
                                        " in ",
                                        as.character(property_info$municipality),
                                        "). Individual model effects are multiplicative adjustments relative ",
                                        "to the standardised reference property. Valuations are reported in million DKK."),
                      label = paste0("illustrative_decomposition_", tolower(property))) %>%
    kable_styling(full_width = FALSE,
                  position = "center",
                  latex_options = c("hold_position"),
                  font_size = 8) %>%

    pack_rows("Reference and valuation date", 1, 2, bold = TRUE) %>%
    pack_rows("Location adjustments", 3, 15, bold = TRUE) %>%
    pack_rows("Structural adjustments", 16, 24, bold = TRUE) %>%
    pack_rows("Aggregate adjustments and valuation", 25, 28, bold = TRUE)


  list(data = property_data,
       latex = latex_table,
       description = property_description)
  
}
```

## 3.4 Predictive performance
The code below extracts various residual types and calculates different performance measures for the training and validation set. Note that using N-fold cross-validation means that there are N-1 estimates for each training point, and the training error is simply taken as the average over these. 


```{r Performance property sales, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Extract predictions and residuals from a cross-validation ensemble
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

get_residuals <- function(models,
                          dataset,
                          specification,
                          fold_from_name = TRUE) {

  if (is.null(names(models))) {names(models) <- paste0("Model", seq_along(models))}

  residual_list <- future_lapply(seq_along(models),
                                 
    function(i) {

      model_name <- names(models)[i]
      model <- models[[i]]

      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Determine validation fold
      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------

      if (fold_from_name) {

        # Supports names such as "Model1", "Model 1", and "Model1_k4000"
        fold <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(sub("^Model\\s*(\\d+).*$", "\\1", model_name)))

      } else {

        fold <- i

      }

      if (is.na(fold)) {stop(sprintf("Could not determine the validation fold from model name '%s'.", model_name))}


      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Prepare prediction data
      #
      # Factor levels are forced to match those stored in the fitted model.
      # This is particularly important for the parametric benchmark, which
      # contains municipality fixed effects and several categorical variables.
      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------

      newdata <- dataset

      if (!is.null(model$xlevels)) {

        for (v in names(model$xlevels)) {

          if (!v %in% names(newdata)) {
            stop(sprintf("Variable '%s' required by model '%s' is missing from the prediction dataset.", v, model_name))
          }

          original_values <- as.character(newdata[[v]])

          unknown_levels <- setdiff(unique(original_values[!is.na(original_values)]), model$xlevels[[v]])

          if (length(unknown_levels) > 0) {

            warning(sprintf(paste0("Specification '%s', model '%s': variable '%s' contains ",
                                   "%d level(s) not present when the model was fitted: %s"),
                    specification,
                    model_name,
                    v,
                    length(unknown_levels),
                    paste(unknown_levels, collapse = ", ")))
          }

          newdata[[v]] <- factor(original_values, levels = model$xlevels[[v]])
          
        }
      }


      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Predict
      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------

      predicted_sales_price <- as.numeric(predict(model, newdata = newdata, type = "response"))

      if (length(predicted_sales_price) != nrow(dataset)) {

        stop(sprintf(paste0("Prediction length mismatch for specification '%s', model '%s': ",
                            "%d predictions for %d observations."),
             specification,
             model_name,
             length(predicted_sales_price),
             nrow(dataset)))
      }

      if (any(!is.finite(predicted_sales_price))) {

        warning(sprintf("Specification '%s', model '%s' produced %d non-finite predictions.",
                specification,
                model_name,
                sum(!is.finite(predicted_sales_price))))
        
      }


      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Residuals
      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------

      tibble(sales_price = dataset$sales_price,
             sales_date_numeric = dataset$sales_date_numeric,
             predicted_sales_price = predicted_sales_price,
             residual_sales_price = predicted_sales_price - dataset$sales_price,
             residual_sales_price_percent = 100 * (predicted_sales_price - dataset$sales_price) / dataset$sales_price,
             residual_sales_price_log = log(predicted_sales_price) - log(dataset$sales_price),
             ratio = predicted_sales_price / dataset$sales_price,
             validation = dataset$validation_set == fold,
             validation_set = dataset$validation_set,
             id = dataset$id,
             municipality_type = dataset$municipality_type,
             Model = paste("Model", fold),
             Specification = specification)
    }
  )

  bind_rows(residual_list)
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Extract residuals for all three specifications
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

residual_df_parametric <- get_residuals(models = models_parametric,
                                        dataset = dataset_property_sales_cv,
                                        specification = "Parametric model")

residual_df_gam1 <- get_residuals(models = models_gam1,
                                  dataset = dataset_property_sales_cv,
                                  specification = "Nationwide GAM")

residual_df_gam2 <- get_residuals(models = models_gam2,
                                  dataset = dataset_property_sales_cv,
                                  specification = "Municipality-type GAM")


residual_df_all <- bind_rows(residual_df_parametric, residual_df_gam1, residual_df_gam2) %>%
                   mutate(dataset_type = if_else(validation, "Validation", "Training"),
                          dataset_type = factor(dataset_type, levels = c("Training", "Validation")),
                          Specification = factor(Specification, levels = c("Parametric model", "Nationwide GAM", "Municipality-type GAM")),
                          municipality_type = factor(municipality_type, levels = c("Capital", "Commuter", "Large city", "Provincial", "Rural")))


# Save residual data
saveRDS(residual_df_all, "saved_files/residual_df_all.rds")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Performance calculation
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

calculate_performance <- function(data) {

  median_ratio <- median(data$ratio)

  tibble(N = nrow(data),
         MALE = mean(abs(data$residual_sales_price_log)),
         MAPE = mean(abs(data$residual_sales_price_percent)),
         MAE = mean(abs(data$residual_sales_price)),
         PM20 = 100 * mean(abs(data$residual_sales_price_percent) <= 20),
         COD = 100 * mean(abs(data$ratio - median_ratio)) / median_ratio,
         PRD = mean(data$ratio) / (sum(data$predicted_sales_price) / sum(data$sales_price)))
}

                           group_modify(~ calculate_performance(.x)) %>%

                                  PRD = round(PRD, digits = 2),
                                  Specification = factor(Specification, levels = c("Parametric model", "Nationwide GAM", "Municipality-type GAM")),
                                  dataset_type = factor(dataset_type, levels = c("Training", "Validation"))) %>%
                           arrange(Specification, dataset_type)
```

## 3.5 Preditiction uncertainty and stability
The code below flags outliers based on both the GAM-based uncertainty estimate of Model 1 as well as the ensemble-based robustness measure described in the main paper. 

```{r Uncertainty detection, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, results = 'hide'}

# The code below identifies statistically fragile valuations using two
# complementary uncertainty measures:
#
#   sigma_Model1   : prediction uncertainty from Model 1
#   sigma_Ensemble : variation in predictions across the four fitted models
#
# A valuation is flagged when either measure exceeds the specified threshold,
# corresponding to the max-rule described in the main paper.


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Predictions and Model 1 uncertainty
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

predictions <- imap(models_gam2,
                    
  function(model, name) {

    preds <- predict.gam(model, dataset_properties, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
    tibble(!!paste0("pred_", name) := as.vector(preds$fit), !!paste0("sigma_", name) := as.vector(preds$se.fit))
    
  }
)


pred_matrix <- bind_cols(predictions)

property_predictions <- bind_cols(dataset_properties, pred_matrix)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Ensemble uncertainty and combined uncertainty
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

pred_cols <- grep("^pred_", names(property_predictions), value = TRUE)

sigma_limit <- 0.20


property_predictions <- property_predictions %>%
                        rowwise() %>%
                        mutate(sigma_Ensemble = sd(c_across(all_of(pred_cols))),
                               sigma_combined = pmax(sigma_Model1, sigma_Ensemble),
                               above_limit = sigma_combined > sigma_limit) %>%
                        ungroup()


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Determine which uncertainty measure causes each flag
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

property_predictions <- property_predictions %>%
                        mutate(flag_source = case_when(!above_limit ~ "Not flagged",
                                                       sigma_Model1 > sigma_limit & 
                                                       sigma_Ensemble > sigma_limit ~ "Both",
                                                       sigma_Ensemble > sigma_limit ~ "Ensemble",
                                                       sigma_Model1 > sigma_limit ~ "Model 1"),
                               flag_source = factor(flag_source, 
                                                    levels = c("Not flagged", 
                                                               "Model 1", 
                                                               "Ensemble", 
                                                               "Both")))


flagged_properties <- property_predictions %>% filter(above_limit)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Summary of flagged properties
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

n_total <- nrow(property_predictions)

n_flagged <- nrow(flagged_properties)

pct_flagged <- 100 * n_flagged / n_total


flag_summary <- property_predictions %>%
                count(flag_source, name = "N") %>%
                mutate(Percent = 100 * N / n_total)

print(flag_summary)


cat("\nFlagged:", format(n_flagged, big.mark = ","), "/", format(n_total, big.mark = ","), sprintf("(%.2f%%)\n", pct_flagged))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Joint distribution of the two uncertainty measures
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

label_expr <- sprintf(paste0("atop(",
                             "'Flagged: %s / %s (%.2f%%)', ",
                             "'Rule: max(' * sigma['Model 1'] * ', ' * sigma[Ensemble] * ') > %.2f'",
                             ")"),
                      format(n_flagged, big.mark = ","),
                      format(n_total, big.mark = ","),
                      pct_flagged,
                      sigma_limit)


plot_uncertainties <- ggplot(property_predictions,
                      aes(x = sigma_Model1, y = sigma_Ensemble)) +
  
                      geom_point(alpha = 0.10,
                                 size = 0.8,
                                 color = "#08306B") +

                      geom_point(data = flagged_properties,
                                 shape = 21,
                                 fill = NA,
                                 color = "#08306B",
                                 size = 1.5,
                                 stroke = 0.7,
                                 alpha = 1) +
```

### Concurvity Analysis
The code investigates concurvity between the various smooths for Model 1 based on https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/mgcv/html/concurvity.html. 

```{r Concurvity analysis, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, results = 'hide', fig.width=20, fig.height=30}

cc <- concurvity(models_gam2$Model1, full = FALSE)

collapse_concurvity <- function(conc_mat, pretty_names) {
  
  # remove self-concurvity first
  diag(conc_mat) <- NA
  
  # base smooth names (strip :municipality_typeXXXX)
  base_names <- sub(":municipality_type.*$", "", colnames(conc_mat))
  uniq_terms <- unique(base_names)
  
  # prepare new collapsed matrix
  conc_grouped <- matrix(NA_real_,
                         nrow = length(uniq_terms),
                         ncol = length(uniq_terms),
                         dimnames = list(uniq_terms, uniq_terms))
  
  # fill blocks
  for (i in seq_along(uniq_terms)) {
    for (j in seq_along(uniq_terms)) {
      rows <- base_names == uniq_terms[i]
      cols <- base_names == uniq_terms[j]
      block <- conc_mat[rows, cols, drop = FALSE]
      conc_grouped[i, j] <- max(block)
    }
  }
  
  # drop parametric part
  conc_grouped <- conc_grouped[
    rownames(conc_grouped) != "para",
    colnames(conc_grouped) != "para",
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  
  # apply nice labels
  rownames(conc_grouped) <- pretty_names[rownames(conc_grouped)]
  colnames(conc_grouped) <- pretty_names[colnames(conc_grouped)]
  
  as.data.frame(conc_grouped)
}
```
